extraction.name: Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models
extraction.description: Introduction of the pointer sentinel mixture architecture for neural sequence models and the WikiText corpus for language modeling.
extraction.creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The WikiText dataset was constructed by selecting Wikipedia articles fitting Good or Featured article criteria. Text was extracted using the Wikipedia API. Specific sections featuring lists were removed, and minor bugs like sort keys and Edit buttons were removed. Mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with tokens. Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer. A vocabulary was constructed by discarding words with a count below 3.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Words were lower-cased, numbers were replaced with N, newlines were replaced with <eos>, and punctuation was removed for Penn Treebank. For WikiText, mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with <formula> tokens. Words outside the vocabulary were mapped to the <unk> token.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text extracted from Wikipedia markup. Sections with lists removed. Minor bugs removed. Normalization and tokenization using Moses tokenizer. Vocabulary construction by discarding words with count below 3. Mapping out-of-vocabulary words to <unk> token.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to improve handling of rare words and usage of long term dependencies in language modeling, addressing limitations of previous datasets like Penn Treebank which lacked realistic vocabularies and long tails.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset consists of Wikipedia articles selected for being well written, factually accurate, broad in coverage, neutral in point of view, and stable. This selection process may introduce biases inherent in Wikipedia's editorial standards and coverage.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The Penn Treebank dataset has limitations including lower-cased tokens, stripped punctuation, and a limited vocabulary of 10k words, making it unrealistic for real language use with large vocabularies and rare words. The WikiText dataset addresses some of these but is still derived from Wikipedia.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning for language modeling tasks.
